title: The Cold Asset Anew
premise: Juniper Quintana, a sleepless interpreter for a fragile peace delegation, discovers that Flight 4471 — carrying a whistleblower who could expose a covert training network — has been erased from every record while still airborne. As the summit approaches, she realizes the network embedded in the delegation itself will kill again to keep its secrets, and that her own missing memories of 'the incident' are the key they fear. Hunting the truth through erased archives, dead contacts, and her own fractured recollection, she uncovers that she was trained by the network years ago and wiped. In the end, Juniper broadcasts the evidence during the summit's opening session, burning the network at the cost of her career and her last illusions about the people she trusted.
about_author: Wendell Okafor is a former conference interpreter turned novelist who spent a decade working behind glass booths in Geneva, Nairobi, and The Hague. He writes thrillers about the people who translate other people's lies for a living.

chapters.title: Booth Nine
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. During a tense pre-summit briefing in Geneva, Juniper interprets a delegation speech and notices a delegate use a phrase that triggers something buried in her memory. She hasn't slept through the night since an incident she can't fully recall. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professionalism; the reader feels her exhaustion and suppressed alarm.

chapters.title: Flight 4471
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. A whistleblower named Ademola Osei, scheduled to testify at the summit, boards Flight 4471 to Geneva. Mid-flight, Juniper watches his flight vanish from tracking sites, then from airline systems, then from news feeds — while radar chatter suggests it's still aloft. Emotional beat: vertigo; reality itself becomes untrustworthy, mirroring her own unreliable memory.

chapters.title: The Erasure Protocol
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper, with a brief interlude from security chief Ilse Brandt. Juniper confronts the delegation's security officer, who denies any anomaly and suggests she take medical leave. She finds Osei's name scrubbed from the witness list he himself submitted. Emotional beat: gaslighting; the machinery of denial closes around her like a door.

chapters.title: What the Incident Was
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Digging through her own past, Juniper finds gaps: a two-year employment record sealed under confidentiality, a language school that never existed. A retired colleague hints she once worked for a contractor called Meridian Group. Emotional beat: grief; the person she thought she was begins to dissolve.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't on the Manifest
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Juniper and Osei (alive, hiding). Osei survived a staged crash cover-up and contacts Juniper using a phrase only Meridian trainees would know — proving she's one of them. He gives her a fragment of encrypted data before going dark. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; trust extended across a chasm of shared guilt.

chapters.title: Counterweight
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Ilse offers Juniper protection in exchange for silence, revealing the network has assets inside the summit's organizing committee. Juniper pretends to accept while copying Ilse's access credentials. Emotional beat: cold calculation; loyalty curdles into strategy as survival demands betrayal.

chapters.title: The Training House
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Following the encrypted fragment to a decommissioned facility outside Lyon, Juniper recovers flashes of her own training — interrogation drills, language-forged identities, sanctioned disappearances — and understands 'the incident' was her refusal to erase a witness like Osei. Emotional beat: horror of self-recognition; the hunter learns she was the weapon.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: POV: multiple, converging. With delegates arriving, the network moves to trigger a staged incident that will collapse the peace process and bury Meridian forever. Juniper decodes Osei's full file but is caught by Ilse, who reveals her own history as a Meridian asset trying to buy her way out. Emotional beat: suffocating pressure; every exit is wired.

chapters.title: Open Session
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. During the summit's live opening, with interpretation piped to forty delegations, Juniper hijacks the audio feed and broadcasts Osei's evidence — flight records, training rosters, her own voice on old Meridian tapes. Security storms the booth as the world listens. Emotional beat: cathartic climax; truth spoken aloud in every language at once.

chapters.title: The Cold Asset, Anew
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper, weeks later. The network is burned, inquiries launched, the summit salvaged on thinner terms than anyone hoped. Juniper testifies, loses her clearance, and finally sleeps through the night — waking not healed, but whole enough. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; survival's price paid, memory reclaimed, identity rebuilt from honest wreckage.
